Gorlos-phos: addressing the stereoselectivity in
palladium-catalyzed exo-mode cyclization of allenes
with a nucleophilic functionality †
Juntao Y e,a Suhua Lia and Shengming Ma* a,b
A novel catalyst system has been indenti ﬁed for addressing the long-standing issue of Z/E stereo-
selectivity in palladium-catalyzed exo-mode cyclization reactions of allenes bearing a nucleophilic func-
tionality with organic halides or their equivalents. The readily accessible, sterically hindered
monophosphine ligand Gorlos-Phos·HBF
4 imparts a remarkable stereocontrolling ability with broad gen-
erality under Pd catalysis.
One of the long-standing and major challenges that organic
chemists face is how to control the chemo-, regio- and stereo-
selectivity of a chemical reaction. 1 Allenes are a class of com-
pounds endowed with a unique reactivity due to the presence
of two consecutive C vC bonds, both of which are highly reac-
tive under appropriate conditions and thus provide opportu-
nities for multiple elaborations; however, they also pose a
great challenge to control the selectivity in their reactions.
2
Among the extensive transformations of allenes, palladium-
catalyzed cyclization reactions of allenes bearing a nucleophi-
lic moiety with organic halides or their equivalents represent
one of the most powerful tools for constructing a wide variety
of carbo- and heterocycles via endo -o r exo-mode cyclization
reactions (Scheme 1).
3 While much attention has been paid to
the enantioselectivity issue in both cases for the synthesis of
optically active compounds via an axial-to-central chirality
transfer process,
3b control of the Z/E stereoselectivity referred
to the exo-mode cyclization (R 1 ≠ H) remains a challenge
(Scheme 1), 4,5 primarily owing to the enormous di ﬃculty in
identifying a catalyst system having eﬃciency in both reactivity
and stereoselectivity. Herein, we report a highly e ﬃcient and
reliable strategy to solve such a challenging issue of Z/E stereo-
selectivity by taking advantage of the readily accessible, steri-
cally hindered monophosphine ligand Gorlos-Phos·HBF4.6a
The reaction of 4-monosubstituted 2,3-allenyl amine 1a
with propargylic carbonate 2a aﬀorded the corresponding
cyclization product 3aa as a mixture of Z/E stereoisomers with
a ratio of Z/E = 82 : 18 (Table 1, entry 1). 4d Thus, we started to
develop a new protocol addressing the issue of Z/E-selectivity
by choosing an appropriate combination of palladium catalyst
and phosphine ligand with di ﬀerent electronic and/or steric
nature (Table 1). When di ﬀerent palladium catalysts (Table 1,
entries 2 –5) were used in combination with TFP (TFP = tri(2 ′-
furyl)phosphine), Pd
2(dba)3·CHCl3 gave the best results in
terms of both the yield and stereoselectivity of 3aa (Table 1,
entry 5). The electron-rich nature of TFP led us to consider
PCy
3, P(1-naphthyl) 3, L1, and L2; however, they all gave inferior
results (Table 1, entries 6 –9). Thus, we reasoned that a steric
eﬀect may also count. Recently, we have developed several
readily available sterically hindered monophosphine ligands
(LB-Phos·HBF4 and Gorlos-Phos·HBF4, Table 1) and found nice
applications in C –Cl bond activation. 6 When these ligands
were tested in this reaction, interestingly, only ( Z)-3aa was
found, as judged by 1H NMR spectroscopic analysis of the
crude reaction mixture with Gorlos-Phos·HBF4 (Table 1, entry
11). Control experiments using its neutral counterpart
Gorlos-Phos gave similar results (Table 1, entry 12), indicating

Under this set of optimal conditions, the substrate scope
was examined (Table 2). To our delight, 2,3-allenyl amines con-
taining a c-hexyl, i-Pr (Table 2, entries 1 –6) or a linear alkyl
substituent (Table 2, entries 7 –10) at the 4-position all
aﬀorded the corresponding products ( Z)-3 as a single isomer
in good to excellent yields. The structure and the configuration
of the C vC bond of these products were confirmed unambigu-
ously by the X-ray di ﬀraction study of ( Z)-3da (Fig. 1).
7
Next, we examined the feasibility of extending the present
system to reactions of 2,3-allenyl amines with organic halides
instead of propargylic carbonates. Gratifyingly, when the reac-
tions of 2,3-allenyl amines and phenyl iodide were carried out
under the aforementioned standard conditions in the presence
of a CO
2 balloon, the corresponding 5-alkenyloxazolidin-2-
ones 4 were also obtained in good to excellent yields with Z/E
ranging from ≥94 : 6 to >97 : 3 as determined using 1H NMR
analysis of the crude reaction mixture (Table 3). The structure
and the configuration of the C vC bond of these products were
confirmed by the X-ray di ﬀraction study of ( Z)-4c (Fig. 2).
8
To further explore the generality of this catalyst system, the
reactions of 4,5-allenoic acids 5 and propargylic carbonates 2
were surveyed and the representative results are shown in
Table 4. To our delight, the reactions of 4,5-allenoic acids 5a–
5c with various propargylic carbonates all furnished the corres-
ponding (Z)-5-(1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl)-4,5-dihydro-2(3H)-furanones

Having achieved the stereoselective synthesis of ( Z)-5-(1,3,4-
alkatrien-2-yl)oxazolidin-2-ones 3, we wondered whether their
chiral counterparts could be obtained by employing the axially
chiral 2,3-allenyl amines
9 via an axial-to-central chirality trans-
fer process. However, when enantioenriched 2,3-allenyl amine
(S)-1a (98% ee) was subjected to the standard conditions, the
corresponding product ( R,Z)-3aa was obtained with only 80%
ee, indicating a serious racemization (Table S1, entry 1, in the
ESI†). Gratifyingly, after extensive study, we eventually found
that the reaction temperature had a significant influence on
the chirality transfer process (Table S1, entries 2 –4†), and
enantioenriched 5-(1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl)oxazolidin-2-one ( R,Z)-3
can be accessed in moderate to good yields with only a slight
decrease in enantiomeric purity at lower reaction temperatures
ranging from 45 to 60 °C (Table 5, entries 1 and 3 –6). The reac-
tion of 2,3-allenyl amine ( S)-1a with cyclic propargylic carbon-
ate 2b was carried out at 70 °C for the full conversion of ( S)-1a
(Table 5, entry 2).
A possible mechanism involving the two di ﬀerent types of
intermediates shown in Scheme 2 was proposed. 4d Path a
involves the formation of a π-allyl palladium species Int 3 via
carbopalladation whereas path b a ﬀords the product 3 via anti-
oxypalladation of Int 4 followed by reductive elimination. As
the enantioenriched 2,3-allenyl amines are capable of transfer-
ring the axial chirality into the newly formed stereogenic
center of 5-(1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl)oxazolidin-2-ones without
obvious loss of enantiomeric purity, we are in favor of path
b since racemization may occur through a σ–π–σ process if the
π-allyl palladium species Int 3 is involved via path a.
3,10 The
steric bulky nature of the ligand Gorlos-Phos helps to increase
the steric di ﬀerence between Int 4 and Int 5 , making the for-
mation of Int 4 more favorable. Therefore, Z isomers were
obtained via Int 4 ( path b). The absolute configurations of the
enantioenriched 5-(1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl)oxazolidin-2-ones were

Conclusions
In conclusion, we have developed an e ﬃcient and highly
stereoselective protocol for the construction of synthetically
attractive oxazolidin-2-one 11 and γ-butyrolactone12 scaﬀolds
with the challenging issue of Z/E stereoselectivity being nicely
addressed by taking advantage of the readily accessible, steri-
cally hindered monophosphine ligand Gorlos-Phos·HBF4. The
simplicity, high stereocontrolling ability as well as promising
generality of this catalyst system clearly demonstrated its vast
potential for stereoselective synthesis in palladium-catalyzed
exo-mode cyclization reactions of allenes bearing a nucleophi-
lic functionality with organic halides or their equivalents.
Further studies are aimed at achieving a better understanding
of the mechanism and applying such a catalyst system in
related transformations.
